results.input: What's the difference between a fixed rate and a floating rate home loan package?
results.response:
**Fixed rate package:** The interest rate stays the same for a set period, so you're protected against rate increases and can budget your monthly payments more easily [4][5]. The trade-offs are that early redemption charges are often imposed during the fixed period, and if market rates fall, you may end up paying a comparatively higher rate [5]. Once the fixed period ends, the rate becomes a floating rate [1].

**Floating rate package:** The interest rate can change periodically, often in relation to a reference rate. When that reference rate moves, your payments may go up or down [5]. DBS's floating packages are based on either:
- **3M SORA**, which reflects the average of actual overnight interbank borrowing rates in Singapore over the last 3 months. It is published daily on the MAS website [2][7][9].
- **FHR (Fixed Deposit Home Rate)**, which is pegged to the bank's own fixed deposit rate. Changes are at the bank's discretion in response to market conditions [2][5][7].

DBS also offers an Easy Switch Loan for completed properties, which starts with a fixed rate and lets you switch to 3M SORA any time after disbursement [1].

For current rates, DBS asks you to contact them [1]. Any rates you see may differ from the one you'd actually be offered. If you'd like, tell me whether you're buying, refinancing or repricing, and I can share the package details on those pages.

results.input: Is there a cap on how much unsecured credit I can have across all banks?
results.response:
Yes. There is an industry-wide borrowing limit on credit card, charge card and unsecured balances, added up across all financial institutions in Singapore [1]. It doesn't apply to unsecured loans for education, business and medical purposes [1].

**How it works**
- The limit is based on your monthly income. It's calculated by taking your total interest-bearing unsecured outstanding balance across all financial institutions and dividing it by your monthly income [3].
- It was lowered in stages: 24 times monthly income from 1 June 2015, 18 times from 1 June 2017, and 12 times from 1 June 2019 [3].

**If you go over the limit**
If your total interest-bearing unsecured balance exceeds the limit (as per DBS's records) for 3 consecutive months, DBS would not allow you to [3]:
- charge new amounts to your existing cards or use unsecured credit facilities issued by DBS
- obtain new cards or unsecured facilities from DBS
- get credit limit increases on existing cards or unsecured facilities issued by DBS

There's no set time limit to bring your balances down. Once they're below the limit, you can approach DBS for a review of your credit situation [8]. You still need to keep up with your payments in the meantime [8].

For how this applies to your own situation, you can check the official DBS page or speak to a banker.

results.input: Can you show me the rules for TDSR?
results.response:
Here are the TDSR rules as published on the MAS and DBS pages I have (as of 27 Oct 2026):

**What it is**
- TDSR is the portion of your gross monthly income that goes towards repaying all your monthly debt obligations, including the loan you're applying for. [2][6]

**The limit**
- No more than 55% of your gross monthly income should go towards all your debt obligations, including the new loan. [4][3]
- This applies to property loans where the OTP is granted on or after 16 December 2021. [3]
- Existing debts count towards the limit. For example, if existing monthly debt obligations equal 10% of your income, the maximum property loan is based on the remaining 45%. [3]

**When it applies**
- It must be calculated for any loan to purchase a property, any loan secured by a property, and the refinancing of these loans. [5]
- It applies to individuals, but not to loans to companies, which are assessed under different criteria. If you're a sole proprietor, or set up a company solely to buy property, TDSR is applied to you as an individual. [5]

**Good to know**
- Banks can adopt more conservative practices than the MAS minimum. [2]
- In some situations, monthly repayments on an existing residential property loan can be excluded when you take a second loan to buy a property, if you meet certain conditions. I don't have the full list of conditions, so please check the MAS page or speak to a banker. [2]
- For DBS home loan repricing of an investment property or owner-occupied property with cash out (term loan), you can alternatively go through a Debt Reduction Plan instead of a TDSR assessment, by repaying at least 3% of the total outstanding loan upfront or over not more than 3 years. [10]

For HDB flats and ECs, a separate MSR limit of 30% of gross monthly income also applies to property loans. [4][8]

Sources: MAS [Calculating TDSR](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/explainers/tdsr-for-property-loans/calculating-tdsr) and [MSR and TDSR Rules](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/explainers/new-housing-loans/msr-and-tdsr-rules).

results.input: What is SORA and how does it affect my home loan?

SORA (Singapore Overnight Rate Average) is the volume-weighted average rate of borrowing transactions in the unsecured overnight interbank SGD cash market in Singapore, between 8am and 6.15pm. It is administered by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and published at 9am on the next business day [2]. **How it affects your home loan**

- If your loan's interest rate is pegged to SORA, it is a floating rate. SORA changes daily, so your loan repayments will change too [4].
- When the reference rate changes, payments may increase or decrease accordingly [10].
- 3M SORA may rise or fall with market interest rates and economic conditions [6].
- Your rate is usually 3M SORA plus a spread. For example, DBS's Green Home Loan pre-determined SORA package shows 3M SORA + 0.28% for Years 1-2, as published on 27 Oct 2026. This package is available only for eligible Green Mark properties [3][9]. Your actual rate may differ [9].

**Why it matters for your home loan**

- **There's a cap.** MAS sets the TDSR threshold at a maximum of 55% of your monthly income for property loans where the OTP was granted on or after 16 Dec 2021 [1]. DBS applies this cap to all borrowers' gross monthly income [4].
- **Your existing debts reduce what you can borrow.** For example, if your existing monthly debts equal 10% of your monthly income, the most you can get for a property loan is based on 45% of your monthly income [1].
- **It applies broadly.** TDSR must be calculated for any loan to purchase a property, any loan secured by a property, and the refinancing of these loans [7]. It applies to individuals, not to loans for companies [7].

**HDB flats and ECs**

If you're buying an HDB flat, there's also a Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR), capped at 30% of gross monthly income [4]. It only counts property loans, and it applies to HDB flats and ECs [6].

**Exclusions in certain situations.** MAS says that if you have an existing residential property loan and are taking a second loan to buy a property, the repayments on the existing property can be excluded from the TDSR calculation in certain situations. You have to meet specific conditions and provide supporting documents [1]. **Stamp duty.** If you're a Singapore Citizen buying a second property, Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) applies. It must be paid upfront and can't be funded by a home loan, though you can use CPF [7].

These are general rules, not an assessment of your situation. A DBS banker can look at your actual numbers.
